title: To better understand the mechanisms enabling malaria parasites to circulate in the blood without causing symptoms, we performed transcriptomic analysis of blood from 44 Ghanaian children: 12 children with symptomatic P. falciparum infection, 25 with asymptomatic P. falciparum malaria, and 7 healthy uninfected children.
description: Blood transcriptomics is a powerful and sensitive tool for characterising the host response to infection. The transcriptome of blood leukocytes reflects both cell-intrinsic responses to pathogens and the effect of cell-extrinsic stimuli, such as cytokines that are released into circulation. To better understand the mechanisms enabling malaria parasites to circulate in the blood without causing symptoms, we performed transcriptomic analysis of blood from 44 Ghanaian children: 12 children with symptomatic P. falciparum infection, 25 with asymptomatic P. falciparum malaria, and 7 healthy uninfected children.

samples.title: SYM-3
samples.description: Children age 6 to 12 years were recruited in Obom, a high Plasmodium falciparum transmission community in the Ga South Municipality of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana, as reported previously. The study participants comprised three groups: children with symptomatic malaria (n=12), children with asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum infection (n=25) and healthy children without infection (n=7)
